# Release 0 contract fixture corpus

`bin/*.bin` contains committed raw binary fixture bundles. Each bundle uses a test-only 64-byte `R0FXBIN\0` envelope followed by exact raw Boot Entry, handoff, memory-map, and RHD byte sequences. The envelope carries fixture lengths, expected result, provider-fault selector, and the independent architecture-adapter conformance tuple; it is not a RAR OS public contract.

`generate.sh` deterministically recreates every binary from `cases.v1`. `run.sh` compares regenerated bytes with the committed corpus. In the pinned Linux CI route, `reference.rs` is compiled as unsafe-free host-only code and validates the raw bytes with checked unsigned arithmetic. It never dereferences fixture addresses or performs device access.

The binary corpus covers valid x86-64/APIC/16550-I/O and AArch64/GICv3/PL011 values plus malformed framing, alignment, overlap, provider faults, critical records, identity, references, memory maps, controller-relative interrupts, typed register windows, address spaces, authority binding, map/RHD consistency, and architecture agreement.

`validation-precedence.v1` declares one deterministic mutation for every one of the 37 artifact-qualified predicates, all 36 adjacent edges, and eight security-sensitive non-adjacent fault pairs. The complete 37-single/36-adjacent matrix runs independently against both x86-64 and AArch64 baselines. `conformance-scenarios.v1` executes 120 cases covering entry/adapter binding and malformed widths/page sizes, critical and compatible descriptor additions, total map arithmetic/ownership/containment reduction under reordering, globally reduced RHD compatibility under reordering, descriptor aliasing, known/unknown record ordering, short and faulting providers, representable compatible optional register roles, unknown critical additions, singleton cardinality/model failures, CPU record and hardware identity, checked interrupt bounds/overlap, exact map/RHD authority equality, map limits, register arithmetic overflow, access logs, and rejected effects.

The host oracle uses a descriptor-keyed instrumented provider. It proves the exact permitted access sequence and rejects a second copy of any source. A separate effect sink proves rejected inputs do not clear entropy, activate trace, or construct device authority. Target-decoder agreement remains an R0-003/R0-004 obligation because no target decoder exists in R0-002.
Every raw fixture, focused predicate, adjacent edge, security pair, and scenario executes behind an unwind boundary; any panic is a conformance failure rather than an accepted rejection result.
